name: Canned seafood (canned tuna, canned fish and other tinplate-packed fishery products)
native_basis_label: edible portion, as consumed (wet weight); tinplate-packed
scope_note: Canned/tinplate-packed fishery products (canned tuna, canned fish). Lead binds the tuna/bonito 200; total mercury binds the general fishery 500; inorganic arsenic binds EU fish-other 100 (infant-food row scope-corrected out). Tin IS material here (canned) and binds Mexico canned-fishery 100000. MeHg bounded by tHg; total Cr binds HK fish 1000; Ni/Al screened; Cr-VI not-material.

Pb.basis: edible portion, wet weight. Canned seafood is predominantly canned tuna; Costa Rica tuna/bonito Pb 200 is the strictest sovereign (EU general fish-muscle 300 concurs). Canning does not change the fish-muscle lead basis.

Cd.basis: edible portion, wet weight; general fish-muscle cadmium 50.

tAs.basis: edible portion, wet weight; total arsenic. Singapore canned-fish total-As 1000 (canned-specific scope).

iAs.basis: edible portion, wet weight; inorganic arsenic. EU Reg. 2025/1891 muscle-meat-of-fish (other) iAs 100. (Scope-corrected: the earlier build mispooled an infant complementary-food iAs row here; that row is excluded — the value is unchanged because EU fish-other is also 100.)

tHg.basis: edible portion, wet weight; total mercury. Canned fishery products bind the general fishery/fish mercury ceiling of 500 (Costa Rica; EU crustaceans/molluscs/fish general).

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg). The binding total-mercury ceiling (500) is at or below the lowest applicable sovereign methylmercury ML for canned/general fishery product (MeHg 500-1000), so passing tHg guarantees MeHg compliance; no separate methylmercury ceiling is published. Audit-affirmed (2026-08-14).
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury screen; reflex MeHg speciation cannot exceed the tHg ceiling.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-Hg fishery ceiling (500); no sovereign MeHg ML sits below it
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU; CR; US-FDA; MX; TH; PH; TT; HK

Ni.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a nickel ML for fish or canned fishery products (EU 2024/1987 nickel is plant-food/seaweed only). Screened rather than assigned a mis-based number.
Ni.reference_method: Total-nickel screen (ICP-MS); no sovereign canned-fish Ni ML.
Ni.trigger: periodic nickel screen; flag on anomalous elevation

Sn.basis: edible portion, wet weight; tin. Canned seafood is the one seafood subcategory where tin is material (tinplate migration). Mexico NOM-242 canned-fishery-products tin 100000 (100 mg/kg) is the strictest sovereign; CR/India 200000 and the general canned 250000 ceiling concur as looser context.

Al.rationale: No credible regulator sets an aluminium contaminant ML for seafood or canned seafood; aluminium is background/packaging-derived, managed by intake vs the EFSA/JECFA TWI.
Al.reference_method: Total-aluminium screen (ICP-MS); managed by TWI; no per-food seafood contaminant ML.
Al.trigger: periodic aluminium screen; flag on anomalous elevation

Cr.basis: edible portion, wet weight; total chromium. Canned fish binds the HK Cap 132V fish total-Cr 1000 (India all-fishery 12000 is looser).

Cr-VI.rationale: Cr-VI is bounded by the total-chromium government limit (HK fish 1000); no Cr-VI food ML exists and Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III) in a reducing animal-tissue matrix. Rebuttable if a routed source reports hexavalent chromium in canned seafood.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Bounded by total-chromium government limit; reflex Cr-VI speciation only on anomalously elevated total chromium.
Cr-VI.regulatory_basis: No Cr-VI food ML anywhere; bounded by total chromium (HK fish 1000)
Cr-VI.jurisdictions_checked: EU; Codex; US-FDA; HK; EPA (water only)

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; explicit-id lookup; MeHg speciation-bounded by tHg on animal seafood; seaweed on dry-matter basis)
